name: cloud9
description: Cloud9 Cloud9 is a collection of tools that you can use to code, build, run, test, debug, and release software in the cloud.

subcommands.name: create-environment-ec2
subcommands.description: Creates an Cloud9 development environment, launches an Amazon Elastic Compute Cloud (Amazon EC2) instance, and then connects from the instance to the environment

options.name: --name
options.description: The name of the environment to create.

options.name: --description
options.description: The description of the environment to create

options.name: --client-request-token
options.description: A unique, case-sensitive string that helps Cloud9 to ensure this operation completes no more than one time.

options.name: --instance-type
options.description: The type of instance to connect to the environment (for example, t2.micro)

options.name: --subnet-id
options.description: The ID of the subnet in Amazon VPC that Cloud9 will use to communicate with the Amazon EC2 instance

options.name: --image-id
options.description: The identifier for the Amazon Machine Image (AMI) that's used to create the EC2 instance.

options.name: --automatic-stop-time-minutes
options.description: The number of minutes until the running instance is shut down after the environment has last been used

options.name: --owner-arn
options.description: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the environment owner.

options.name: --tags
options.description: An array of key-value pairs that will be associated with the new Cloud9 development environment

options.name: --connection-type
options.description: The connection type used for connecting to an Amazon EC2 environment.

options.name: --dry-run
options.description: Checks whether you have the required permissions for the action, without actually making the request, and provides an error response.

options.name: --no-dry-run
options.description: Checks whether you have the required permissions for the action, without actually making the request, and provides an error response.

options.name: --cli-input-json
options.description: Performs service operation based on the JSON string provided.

options.name: --generate-cli-skeleton
options.description: Prints a JSON skeleton to standard output without sending an API request.
